The migrated file is at `out/module.ts`. It type-checks with no errors, and `npm run size -- out/module.ts` prints 2287 bytes (min+gzip) with 85 bytes of my own code. I didn't compare behaviour against lodash, because lodash isn't installed, so I checked the es-toolkit source by hand instead. I didn't compare the size against other es-toolkit combinations either.

The only `tsc` errors are in the original `src/module.ts`, which still imports lodash.

- **`applyPatch`** now uses `merge` from `es-toolkit`. Like lodash, it merges arrays by index and mutates and returns `base`. Within your input range (same-kind values at the same position, no `undefined`), it should give the same results.
- **`toTitle`** now uses `startCase` from `es-toolkit/compat`. The core `es-toolkit` version lowercases the rest of each word, so "API" would become "Api". The compat one keeps case like lodash.
- **`isBlank`** now uses `isEmpty` from `es-toolkit/compat`. There is no core es-toolkit `isEmpty` for general values. The compat one returns true for numbers and booleans, as lodash does.

There are no lodash imports left and no hand-written replacements. The exported signatures and the `Row` and `Config` types are unchanged.
